identity.title: Modeling Hierarchical Thinking in Large Reasoning Models

problem.claim: The work addresses how to model and control reasoning trajectories in Large Reasoning Models that generate long Chain-of-Thought sequences.

gap.claim: The dynamics governing LRM reasoning trajectories are not well understood and may produce inconsistencies and reasoning pathologies.

contributions.claim: An FSM representation approximates hierarchical reasoning dynamics through six abstract cognitive states and their transitions.
The authors analyze transition topology to identify statistical shifts associated with effective versus failing reasoning chains.
Q-Value guided steering provides training-free, inference-time control by estimating long-horizon transition utility and applying sparse orthogonal activation steering at sentence boundaries.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present reasoning as a planning problem and introduce Q-Value guided steering to align generation with high-level reasoning policies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the six states and their transitions can be captured in the model's latent state.

Across AIME25, MATH-500, GSM8k, and GPQA Diamond with three open reasoning models, the authors report significant performance gains from Q-Value steering and often 25× fewer interventions than greedy and weighted baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long CoT reasoning is difficult to understand and can exhibit inconsistencies or pathologies.
The authors model hierarchical reasoning as an FSM trajectory over six cognitive states.
They report that the states and transitions appear in latent representations and use transition topology to distinguish effective from failing chains.
They propose Q-Value steering and report benchmark gains with substantially fewer interventions than stated baselines.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a state-transition representation to both failure analysis and inference-time control.

lessons.interpretation: A shared intermediate representation can connect explanation of behavior with a concrete intervention mechanism.
lessons.application: When proposing a control method, define an interpretable trajectory representation and show how its structure motivates the control signal.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when the representation is not empirically tied to model behavior or when added abstraction obscures the target failure mode.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six cognitive states, how latent-state capture is measured, or how effective and failing chains are labeled.
Details of benchmark protocols, statistical significance, baseline configurations, and the meaning of “surgical” efficiency are not provided.
